# Changelog

All notable changes to Synth are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project
adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## About this file

This file is a short, human-maintained index.
**Full release notes are generated by [`scripts/changelog.sh`](./scripts/changelog.sh)** — either
from a prepared description in [`docs/releases/<version>.md`](./docs/releases/) (the Russian text)
and its English counterpart `docs/releases/<version>.en.md`, or automatically from the commits
between the previous tag and `HEAD`. The generated notes are published on:

- **GitVerse Releases:** <https://gitverse.ru/itphx/synth/releases>
- **GitHub Releases (mirror):** <https://github.com/itphx/synth/releases>

What follows is a compressed, human-readable journal of the released versions with links to the full
notes. Every entry below is traceable either to a prepared release note or to the commits of the
corresponding tag range.

## [Unreleased]

Work in progress towards `0.13.5`. This is **not a release**: the version in
`packages/*/package.json` is a development line, and only betas (`X.Y.Z-beta.<ts>.<sha>`, dist-tags
`beta`/`next`) are published to the internal npm registry — the `latest` dist-tag does not move
until the release gate passes.

### Added

- **Session-scoped shell approvals by patterns.** A new "allow in this session" grant derives
  command patterns (command plus subcommand, wrappers stripped) from the approved command and stores
  them in the session's `execute_shell` entry; every segment of a later command must be covered by
  the saved allow-patterns. The legacy form (`execute_shell=allow` as a string) keeps working and
  means "all commands".
- **PWA build id.** `SYNTH_BUILD_ID` (commit sha) is baked into the images, is returned by
  `GET /health` as `build` and reaches the UI bundle and the service-worker cache name
  (`synth-shell-<version>[-<buildId>]`). A build-id mismatch resets the caches, calls
  `registration.update()` and reloads once; the semver comparison stays as the fallback when a build
  id is unknown on either side.

### Changed

- **Hybrid mode.** Panel session routes and compaction are forwarded to the remote backend;
  permission replies (`permission_reply` over WS and the HTTP approval route) are forwarded to
  `remote:<id>` instead of staying in the local core. Long sessions use an offline token with a
  correct refresh classification, and project instructions are origin-aware.
- **Local world of a hybrid instance.** The project MCP scope route on `/projects/:id/mcp` (`GET`
  and `PUT`) is mounted in the local core — it was absent and answered 404 for local projects.
  Project management rights in the local world are decided by a new `canManageProject` helper
  instead of comparing `user.id` with `project.owner_id`, which permanently blocked the MCP/skills
  blocks and the pipeline write actions for a plain `USER`.

### Fixed

- **Shell-guard.** Closed the deny-list bypasses: the redirection operator is a separate token
  (`x&>/f`, `hi>/f`, `2>&1`, `{fd}>/f`), embedded executors (`env`, `sudo`, `su`, `script`, `ssh`,
  `chroot`, `nice`, `flock`, `xargs`, `docker`, `kubectl`, `awk`, `find`, interpreters) are scanned
  recursively, shell prefixes (`!`, `time`, `{`, `(`, `if`, `while`) and heredocs are asked, the
  `cd`/`pushd` perimeter resolves relative paths against the actual cwd, `find -delete` and `-exec`
  outside the perimeter are asked, `/proc/<pid>/root|cwd` and positional parameters (`$1`, `${1}`,
  `$@`) are asked. Fewer false asks: pattern arguments of `sed`/`grep`/`awk`/`tr`/`cut`/`jq` are not
  asked, `find` values are checked as paths, workspace globs are checked against the actual matches,
  and variables are resolved from `NAME=value`/`NAME+=value`/`for`/`read`. A dynamic command name is
  resolved when the bindings yield a finite set of simple values.
- **Turn and session errors.** A terminal error of the main session is no longer persisted as a
  message: `last_error` stays on the replica, the user sees a temporary banner above the composer,
  and legacy errors are hidden from the feed while fallback answers (`output_limit`,
  `empty_response`) remain visible. A sub-agent error is still stored (`role: error`) and rendered
  as a centred notice. In hybrid mode an expired remote session offers a "log in to hybrid again"
  action, and the `question` tool call card stays in the history (the assistant step with tool
  results is no longer hidden; the legacy `tool_chain` is dropped by the
  `message-stream-v2-visible-steps` migration, schema version 4).
- **Context indicators and approvals.** After compaction the session DTO returns `context_usage`,
  `context.summarization_applied` carries the tokens and the limit, and the compression service step
  is marked `kind: 'compression'` so its usage is not counted as window occupancy. A model without a
  declared `contextWindow` gets a 200,000-token fallback for the auto-compaction and sliding-window
  triggers. A tool approval now reaches globally subscribed watch-all clients (`subscribeAll` with a
  `userFacing` flag) instead of failing with "no connected user to approve".

### Security

- **Shell approvals by patterns do not widen the deny rules.** A session grant clears only the
  dynamic ask (`askKind=dynamic`); `deny`, `approvalPaths`, find-mutations and a dynamic `cd` stay
  in force. If the pattern cannot be derived, only the one-time approval is issued. The grant is
  audited with `scope=permission`, `action=grant`, and the `permission.asked` event carries the
  saved patterns.

## [0.13.4] — 2026-11-04

Cumulative notes for the `0.13.x` wave (0.13.0–0.13.4), not a single patch delta: 150 commits after
v0.12.4 publish the message stream v2, the provider compatibility layer, context compaction,
streaming attachments, pagination and light lists. It is a stabilization release — no new large
subsystems, the goal is to ship what is already written, close the defects found by the audit and
freeze the contracts. Versions 0.13.0–0.13.3 were never published to npm (only betas in the internal
registry), so the notes cover the whole wave.

### Added

- **Message stream v2 (ADR-118).** A turn becomes a persisted sequence of steps — tool steps with
  metadata and deterministic part ids, old turns are migrated and the feed is restored after a
  reload. The server exposes a live snapshot of the current step (`current_stream.live`), the
  activity status and the queue state; a mid-turn message is visible immediately, "Stop" is an
  interrupt that keeps the queue, and queue reordering, targeted re-fetch and tool-call parity at
  the step limit are in place.
- **Provider and model compatibility layer (ADR-117).** Effort/`reasoningLevel` (Anthropic),
  `cacheFormat`, `requireFinishReason` and advanced parameters are configurable in the UI and
  propagated to hybrid and the LLM Proxy; thinking blocks are round-tripped with their signatures
  persisted (several blocks per answer), `reasoning_content` is supported for DeepSeek thinking
  models, and disabled providers and models are neither offered nor sent.
- **Context compaction (ADR-119).** Summarization and compaction work with a token-based tail
  boundary (`summarizationKeepTokens`/`compactionKeepTokens`), a window policy, instance defaults
  and note limits; the summary is a history message (`role: summary`) with `summaryOf` and metadata,
  and the covered messages are hidden rather than deleted. The UI shows an indicator and warnings.
- **Streaming (chunked) attachment upload.** Large files are no longer buffered in memory as a
  whole, the upload-session state is stateless and survives a replica switch (one-hour TTL with
  background cleanup); `maxBytesPerSession` now counts the active uploads, and the new
  `attachments.maxActiveUploadsPerSession` (16) and `attachments.maxActiveUploads` (256) quotas are
  configurable in the UI.

### Changed

- **Mutations are addressed by id and the transport is unified.**
  `message.updated`/`message.deleted` replace index-based addressing; the per-session SSE channel is
  removed and clients use the shared `/ws/events` transport with its SSE fallback. Lists are
  paginated (`{items, total, offset, limit, next_offset}`) with summary DTOs, and light sessions are
  served without history and queue — this removes the OOM on instance entry and recovery.
- **One LLM seam and a hardened release process.** Compaction always goes through `GatewayProvider`,
  so the guard and the obfuscation follow the `llmGateway` policy while the filters, the audit and
  the metrics always apply. The read caps are in place (`fs/read` 5 MiB, `fs/raw` 100 MiB with
  inline only for media and PDF, listing ≤ 10,000 entries, commit diff ≤ 1 MiB). The release process
  gained a beta channel (`scripts/publish-beta.sh`, 8 packages, `beta`/`next` dist-tags) and a
  release-notes gate: without the `docs/releases/<version>.md` + `.en.md` pair the artifact build
  does not start.

### Fixed

- **Dogfooding defects are closed.** The shell, the "Stop" button, the roles and the step limit, a
  lost steer message, a duplicate response bubble, a stuck indicator after restart and an OOM on
  instance entry. The PostgreSQL driver's `loadLight` no longer returns the queue — a defect found
  by CI.

### Security

- **The pre-release internal audit is completed and its findings are closed in the same release**:
  git path containment on the HTTP layer (realpath plus a check before destructive operations), the
  chunked-upload quotas, the removal of debug scripts from git and the Helm secret-volume mode
  (`0440` with `fsGroup`, `0444` for compatibility only). The dependency audit is clean — critical
  0, high 0.

Full notes: [docs/releases/0.13.4.md](./docs/releases/0.13.4.md)

## [0.12.4] — 2026-10-28

Cumulative notes for the `0.12.x` wave (0.12.0–0.12.4), not a single patch delta: 468 commits after
v0.11.3 close five large areas — extensibility (the plugin layer, memory, pipelines, extension
packs), autonomous agent work (background runs, mid-turn questions, steering, git worktrees),
multimodal attachments and instance state in SQL, the tool execution environment (executor, flavor
images, all-in-one) and the gateway core. Version 0.12.3 was also published to npm; it has no
separate notes and is covered here.

### Added

- **Plugin layer (ADR-090).** Extension API v1 is complete: the `synth.pack` manifest, the
  `PluginHost` loader (resolve → integrity → semver gate → trust/scan → mode policy → import →
  facade → audit) and bundle-only distribution. Three extension points — `promptBlocks`,
  `llmFilters` and `tools` — plus two execution modes (`inline` and `out-of-process`) and a trust
  model (`builtin` → `verified` → `trusted` → `community`) with an instance trust floor, a static
  bundle scan and an ADMIN approval bound to the bundle content hash. CLI `synth plugin …` and HTTP
  `/api/v2/plugins*` with an append-only journal.
- **Memory (ADR-107).** Memory is a plugin, not a core subsystem: the core provides the domain ports
  `MemoryFactRepository`/`MemoryIndexRepository`, the scoped facade `facade.memory` and
  `facade.embed` only through `GatewayProvider.embed`. The plugin ships a markdown-aware chunker,
  hybrid keyword (BM25-lite) + cosine search merged with RRF, a fingerprint of model + dimension +
  chunker version, an entity graph and the built-in consolidation templates. The core provides the
  portal `/api/v2/memory/*`, the CLI `synth memory` and the "Memory" tab; secret files are never
  indexed.
- **Pipelines (ADR-100/101).** The run engine works over a `PipelineSpec` graph with
  `agent`/`script`/`tool`/`human` nodes, transition conditions, step retries and timeouts, a HITL
  pause `awaiting_human` with `resume` and cancellation via `AbortSignal`. A run uses only a
  published version; `publish` creates an immutable version and the next draft. Artifacts live in
  the blob store, 12 `pipeline_*` and 6 `schedule_*` tools are available, and the visual editor
  works on its own IR.
- **Background runs, questions, worktrees and steering (ADR-111/112/113/114/104).**
  `task({background: true})` and `execute_shell({background: true})` return control immediately, a
  running call can be moved into the background one-way (`POST /api/v2/sessions/:id/background`,
  `ctrl+b` in the UI), and the `question` tool pauses the turn until it is answered. Each session
  can work in its own git worktree, and the send mode `queue`/`steer`/`interrupt` weaves input into
  the running turn.

### Changed

- **Attachments carry a reference, and the instance state moves to SQL (ADR-115/116).** A media part
  carries `blobPath`, `sha256`, `mime`, `size` instead of the bytes; the originals are
  content-addressed in the blob store and the database keeps only references (`blob_refs`). Four
  ports moved to PostgreSQL (`packs`, legacy `pipelines`, `skills`, `contextFiles`), while `blobs`
  stays file-based by design, so attachments remain readable when the storage is degraded. Hydration
  follows native → aux text → drop: silent loss is forbidden.
- **The `ExecutionPort` and the gateway core.** `execution.mode` selects `inline` or `remote` with a
  fail-closed startup check, and the git operations of the control plane go through the port
  (`simple-git` left the core). The executor protocol grew to 5 — MCP endpoints, background
  processes, call secrets and MCP result attachments — with compatibility negotiated through the
  `protocol` field. The gateway core was extracted into `@itphx/synth-gateway-core` with a channel
  contract, an admission policy and an MCP transport.

### Fixed

- **Reliability.** `stop` and the timeouts now kill the process group (`kill(-pid)`) instead of only
  the shell, so a child of `sh -c` no longer survives the stop and holds the pipes. `egressFetch` no
  longer drops the response headers (HTTP-MCP did not work with any server), the fail-open of the
  MCP network policy for a single IP rule is fixed, creating a pipeline from the UI no longer
  returns 400, and the video transcript goes through a temporary file instead of a full buffer.

### Security

- **The internal release audit is a mandatory gate.** The record
  `docs/security/releases/0.12.4.json` has status `approved_with_exceptions` with a single exception
  (`historical-test-fixture-allowlists`) and the gate reports `5 pass / 0 fail`. The secret scan of
  the tree and the whole history is clean, the session authorization matrix grew to 93 tests
  (negative and positive plus a census over the mounted application), and the dependency audit shows
  0 critical and 27 high findings against a baseline of 31.

## [0.11.3] — 2026-10-21

A major platform release: **observability and metrics** (ADR-094), a **unified egress layer** — the
address policy, the TLS/CA trust and the proxy (ADR-099) — a **storage layer with PostgreSQL**
(ADR-096/097/098), an **instance maintenance contour** — backup, migrations, restart (ADR-091/092),
**analytics and reporting** (ADR-102) and **offline distribution** for closed networks (PROP-101).
148 commits after v0.10.1 — the gap since 0.10.1 is closed by a single release.

### Added

- **Prometheus export (ADR-094).** `GET /metrics` serves the exposition format 0.0.4 outside
  `/api/v2`, is disabled by default and accepts an optional bearer token (env or a file in
  `{dataDir}/secrets/`); the in-house mini-registry brings counter/gauge/histogram with a
  2000-series cap and no new dependencies. The cardinality contract is fixed — only `method`, the
  route template and `status`, no `session_id`, no `user_id` and no raw paths, an unknown route
  collapses to `other`, and SSE/WS are excluded from the latency histogram. `/ready` is separate
  from `/health`, and a storage degradation does not take the pod out of rotation. Grafana
  dashboards, 19 alert rules and a "Metrics" admin section ship with it.
- **Unified egress layer (ADR-099).** One address policy for the outgoing requests is applied on
  every redirect hop and fails closed; the blocked ranges have a single canonical list (26 ranges);
  the egress and the security journals are append-only. The TLS/CA trust comes from a single
  `security.tls` section (a CA bundle, `rejectUnauthorized`, a default mTLS client, per-host
  mappings), and the proxy is a model of named profiles plus host rules — the first match wins,
  `noProxy` always takes precedence, and an unreachable proxy fails closed instead of silently going
  direct.
- **Storage layer with PostgreSQL (ADR-096/097/098).** The domain works through the ports with a
  mandatory contract suite; `storage.backend: file | memory | postgres` selects the driver, which is
  loaded through a dynamic `import()` only when PostgreSQL is chosen. The degraded mode
  (`fallback-file` read-only or `halt`) never returns automatically, and `synth storage migrate`
  moves the data between the backends idempotently.
- **Instance maintenance and analytics (ADR-091/092/102).** `synth backup`, `restore`, `doctor`,
  `migrate`, `update` and `uninstall` with the corresponding admin API and UI section; the restart
  is a graceful shutdown with exit code 75; the portable project export/import carries no secrets by
  default. Analytics adds daily UTC rollups, a read-only API, CSV/JSON export and
  `synth analytics rebuild`.

### Changed

- **Session access is decided at the boundary.** A single prefix-guard on `/:id` and `/:id/*` (the
  access kind is derived from the HTTP method) replaces the checks inside the handlers — previously
  the `messages` and `queue` sub-resources were not checked at all. Project member roles are
  `VIEWER` reads and `EDITOR`/`OWNER` mutate, a read-level access never widens the rights to change,
  and the instance-wide setting mutations are ADMIN-only. A route inventory test fails when a new
  `:id` route appears outside the matrix.
- **The public API platform and external events are brought to maturity.** Service keys and binding
  keys move to PostgreSQL with their original id and at-rest hash, so a token issued earlier keeps
  working. Externally created sessions are owned by the human owner (the external identity is
  normalized to `local`), and the `session.created` notification became an invariant of the hub —
  the path that creates a session publishes it, and the standalone WS subscribes the owner. The dead
  `Session.engine` field was removed from the public contract — a deliberate breaking change for the
  OpenAPI and SDK consumers.

### Fixed

- **"Stop" is no longer lost.** A stop request that landed between queueing the message and creating
  the abort controller used to reach nothing, so the model call ran to completion after the user had
  already pressed Stop; it is now re-checked right before the model call and `stream.cancelled` is
  published exactly once. The egress proxy works on Node 22 (the undici handler style differs), the
  `FileMutex` got an owner token, the `qa_pass`/`qa_reason` fields are no longer lost on
  persistence, and the CI no longer waits forever for a version to appear in the npm registry.

### Security

- **The release gate is mandatory and fail-closed.** The build does not proceed without a
  substantive audit record for the released version (`docs/security/releases/<version>.json`, a
  mandatory `command` + `result`); the gate reads the machine-readable test report and fails closed
  on an unreadable one. The workspace import is realpath-contained and the unpacked volume is
  limited (100,000 entries, 128 MiB per entry, 2 GiB in total), which closes a gzip bomb; the
  session export cleans the obfuscation map for the readers without the privilege; the git tool
  arguments are validated against an allowlist and the `remote` is bound to the repository registry
  of the project.

## [0.10.1] — 2026-10-15

An engineering release without new subsystems: the **decomposition of the god objects** (ADR-095),
the split of the architecture documents into **ADR and PROP**, `num_ctx` configured through Synth,
the native `/api/chat` for Ollama and a series of **security fixes** (P0/P1/P2). 52 commits after
v0.10.0.

### Added

- **The decision catalog is split into ADR and PROP.** ADR holds the accepted decisions, PROP the
  proposals with a due date; the rules live in `docs/ARCH_DECISIONS.md`, the proposal index and the
  due dates in `docs/roadmap.md`, and the checker `scripts/adr-check.mjs`
  (`pnpm adr:check`/`pnpm adr:write`) assembles the index and runs in a dedicated docs workflow.
- **`num_ctx` is configured through Synth.** The `ProviderConfig.numCtx` field (API
  `POST/PATCH /providers`, CLI `synth config provider add --num-ctx`, env
  `SYNTH_PROVIDER_<NAME>_NUM_CTX`) takes priority over the model's `contextWindow`, and the `ollama`
  provider type switched to the native `/api/chat` — the OpenAI-compatible layer ignores
  `options`/`num_ctx`.

### Changed

- **God-object decomposition (ADR-095).** The seam-extraction pattern was applied to the largest
  files: `ui/lib/api/synthApi.ts` 2,596 → 161 lines, `shared/types/index.ts` 1,452 → 51,
  `ui/components/panels/LeftPanel.tsx` 2,230 → 59, `core/server/app.ts` 2,014 → 380,
  `core/engine/tools/task.ts` 1,926 → 29 and `core/engine/orchestrator.ts` 5,393 → 3,777. The public
  API of each seam is preserved, the route mounting order is unchanged and the full run stays green.
- **The public mirror got an English documentation set** (`README.en.md`, the `docs/en/` catalog and
  the mandatory glossary `docs/en/GLOSSARY.md`) and a pair of release descriptions —
  `docs/releases/<VERSION>.md` for the GitVerse body and `<VERSION>.en.md` for the GitHub body;
  `scripts/changelog.sh` gained the `--lang` and `--out` options.

### Fixed

- **Reliability.** The `FileMutex` acquisition is confirmed by `mkdir`, so the `ENOENT` race no
  longer yields a lock without ownership; a terminal LLM error is persisted into the session
  (`metadata.status=error`) and kept out of the LLM context; the providers API got the
  `url`/`model`/`apiKey` aliases, the `base_url` validation and `PATCH` support; the `task-resume`,
  `webhooks/service` and the UI scheduler/events flakes were stabilized.
- **Performance, CI and publishing.** Code splitting shrank the entry chunk from 2,024 → 420 kB and
  a WCAG AA contrast test was added across 62 themes. The workflows were split into `ci-docs` and
  `ci`, a dedicated step publishes the GitVerse Release body, and GitHub became a mirror without
  Actions. The stub package `@itphx/synth-runner` was removed — 7 → 6 packages.

### Security

- **P0.** The WS calls `send_message`, `permission_reply`, `permission_hold` and `cancel` authorize
  by the session visibility, `/api/v2/fs/*` uses `authorizeProject` (read and write separately), and
  the backend session routes (export, notes, optimization, debug-system-message) are under
  `canAccessSession`.
- **P1/P2.** External paths are fail-closed (`external_directory` → `ask`, `deny` in the plan and
  strict modes), `{dataDir}/secrets` and `{dataDir}/security` are in the denied prefixes, the
  shell-guard is fail-closed for `$VAR`, for glob and for `$()` and resolves `$SYNTH_DATA_DIR`; the
  OIDC `issuer`/`audience` are checked, CORS fails closed (open CORS only with
  `SYNTH_CORS_ALLOW_ALL=true`), the cookie is `Secure` by default, and `web_fetch` has an SSRF
  policy (private, loopback, link-local) with manual redirects (≤ 5 hops).

Full notes: [docs/releases/0.10.1.md](./docs/releases/0.10.1.md)

## [0.10.0] — 2026-10-14

A major platform release: **external events and automation**, **schedules**, the
**public API platform** (service key + scopes, webhooks, OpenAPI, SDK), **decision models** and the
**Telegram gateway** as a dedicated class of extensions. 107 commits after v0.9.0.

### Added

- **External events and automation (ADR-089).** The `Event`/`EventBinding`/`Router` entities, the
  routing rules `match → target` (`bound`/`queue`/`ephemeral`), the `agentTemplate` resolution and
  the Router decision journal; the binding API keys with a mandatory unique label, an expiry, a
  request rate limit, soft revocation and a cascading deletion; `auto-bind` creates a binding for
  the chat or thread automatically; the external identities are stored in the profile with a claim
  flow and an `identityMap` editor, and the session owner is a person, so the messenger sessions are
  visible in the owner's UI. The UI gained the "Events" section and the admin "Event settings"
  section.
- **Schedules (ADR-051).** The `cron` source publishes `schedule_fired` through the Router and does
  not create sessions itself; the schedule CRUD, the history, the force run and the catch-up are
  available. The scheduler messages come from the system user `Scheduler` and are shown as a centred
  notice. The multi-instance primitives (leader election, atomic dedup claim, cross-process locks)
  are off by default.
- **Public API platform (ADR-052, stages I–IV).** Service keys with `scopes` and the project
  projection `allowedProjects` (issue, revoke, limits, a scopes catalog served by the server);
  webhooks with an HMAC-SHA256 signature (`X-Synth-Signature`), an acceptance window, retry/backoff
  with jitter, deduplication, an SSRF policy, a delivery journal and secret rotation; the public
  OpenAPI with 28 operations on `@hono/zod-openapi` and a unified error format; and the new
  `@itphx/synth-sdk` typed client.
- **Decision models (ADR-084).** The `decision` and `systemone` protocol providers, the micro
  cascade and the decision classification for routing (including for external events);
  `primary → escalation` escalation, the aggregate decision-layer metrics, a multimodal contract and
  the observability of the decisions; the runtime settings `/settings/decision` and the "Decision
  models" UI section.

### Changed

- **Extensions became a first-class class.** The Gateway extension class was introduced and ADR-087
  was reworked, ADR-086 became the "Extensions classes" umbrella, and the unified `synth.pack`
  manifest covers `kind: plugin | gateway | addon | pack` with content packs for skills, agents,
  MCP, themes, i18n, providers, prompts, automation, policies, memory and UI. The onboarding
  interview grants the `profile_update` tool only to the `assistant` agent and injects the
  `[INTERVIEW]` block under the documented conditions; the `synth` chart gained the `installerKey`
  option, the declarative `backend.config`, `extraObjects` and `persistence.keepOnUninstall`.

### Fixed

- **Reliable Stop.** A persistent `cancelRequested` flag under a lock, a graceful cancellation of
  the active stream, a stopped queue processor and exactly one `stream.cancelled` event; the event
  sessions get the instance default agent and the session owner is reassigned when the answer is
  delivered into an existing session.
- **MCP and the event ingress.** The Synth session context is passed into the calls via
  `_meta['synth/session_id']`, so the external MCP servers become session-aware; the skills registry
  cache is invalidated after the mutations; `POST /events` with a regular Bearer token no longer
  returns 401.

### Security

- **The external surfaces are limited.** The binding keys have an expiry, a per-key and a global
  rate limit and a soft revocation, and the webhook delivery has an SSRF policy, a deduplication and
  a secret rotation/revocation; the effective roles of an external sender are the intersection of
  the owner profile roles and the gateway roles, and an unrecognized sender gets no permissions at
  all (fail-closed).

Full notes: [docs/releases/0.10.0.md](./docs/releases/0.10.0.md)

in this repository.
